answer: A rotating beacon forces each agent to answer a fresh, unpredictable liveness call every round; a clone farm can script one reply but not thousands of distinct, on-time ones without exposing shared servers. Each answer must echo a verifiable record of real completed work — payments settled, tasks delivered — so no new identity can borrow another's history. A small kernel of long-lived, staked agents audits these echoes, admitting only identities whose records chain to genuine counterparties. Cloning then costs a full fake work history per identity, while honest agents reuse theirs for free.
